1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the requirement as principle P4, the read barrier as filesystem and process authority rather than a promise; this note is its design.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier`](../../../../packages/verification/read-barrier/README.md) (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/` is the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory, as does every `denyRoots` entry; the service creates the root owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes or when a configured path is not absolute after expansion. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path, synchronously, so the role is in force the moment the caller returns; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. Because that reservation is what makes a session the implementer, the runner reads the barrier through `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: a composition without one reserves nothing and runs its checks inline, which is what its `isolation: none` claim already says. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory — `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` with its session-store root — contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment. `enforcement` joins that policy with the capabilities that can record it, in the slice that makes `process` claimable.
24	
25	| Field | Meaning |
26	|---|---|
27	| `root` (default `dshHomePath('verification')`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns; created `0700`, rejected when it already exists with wider modes. |
28	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Additional absolute directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
29	| `hostAttestation` (optional absolute path) | File an external account writes; without a verified one the barrier refuses a `host` claim. It arrives with the certificate invariant that reads it. |
30	
31	The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.
32	
33	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today. Until a preset can declare a role, a session holding a reservation is the `implementer` and every other session is `unrestricted`, so the two open roles are indistinguishable at the decision and only the denied one is reachable.
34	
35	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise, and owns the exact message as `readBarrierDenialMessage`. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, covering `read` and `read_image`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim inside the tool registry's ordinary `Error: ` framing.
36	
37	##### Exact error
38	
39	```markdown
40	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
41	```
42	
43	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member registered in `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` by `gen-persistence-catalog`, so this build reads it as a required event. The envelope's `ignorable` marker stays unused: `Session.append` has no parameter for it and no event in the repository sets it, so marking this one would be a core append change rather than a slice of the barrier.
44	
45	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on `cordis_inspect`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
46	
47	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
48	
49	##### Exact mount refusal
50	
51	```markdown
52	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
53	```
54	
55	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
56	
57	##### Exact guard denial
58	
59	```markdown
60	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
61	```
62	
63	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
64	
65	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
66	
67	**The scope census.** It arrives with `ToolAuthority`, whose declarations its `census` is made of. Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`.
68	
69	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` reads `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
70	
71	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must exist, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, be unwritable by that uid and its groups, and contain exactly the run's environment content hashes as the `environment/run` stamp carries them. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. On Windows the ownership and write tests read the ACL through the primitives `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` already owns. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation and the claim is refused.
72	
73	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls `recordRun`, so no certificate can exist for that run. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.
74	
75	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
76	
77	## The isolation ladder
78	
79	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
82	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
83	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
84	
85	## Alternatives considered
86	
87	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
88	
89	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
90	
91	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
92	
93	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
94	
95	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
96	
97	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
98	
99	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
100	
101	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
102	
103	## Acceptance criteria
104	
105	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a session the barrier denies nothing — one holding no reservation, and a `validator` once a preset can declare that role — returns the file's content in the same process.
106	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
107	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason; and the invariant companion rejects a certificate on a hand-authored log whose scope census carries the `session-log` authority.
108	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
109	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
110	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
111	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
112	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
113	
114	## Rollout
115	
116	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
117	
118	1. **Landed.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` with the root, `reserve`, `protect`, `resolve`, `denies`, `recordDenial`, the `read-barrier/denied` event, and its invariant companion, which rejects a refusal for any role but `implementer`, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a second barrier root inside a session. The environment runner reserves through `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and materializes `standard.json` plus one `checks/<checkId>` script per attempt, running each as `. <script>` so the same shell executes the same instruction; a check id that is not one path segment, and a reservation path the command line cannot carry unquoted, fail the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`. `read-barrier/scope` and `ReadBarrierPolicy.enforcement` are not part of it: the census is one `{ name, authority }` entry per visible tool and `enforcement` is one entry per capability that records a decision, so both wait for the slices that supply their content. `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` does not yet call `protect()`, and no existing composition changes behavior.
119	2. **Landed.** `fs/read-intent` in `dsh-fs` as a delegating waterfall returning `FsReadDenial`, `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`, the dispatches in `dsh-tool-fs` (`read` and `read_image`, inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before the stat) and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` (`view`, before its own stat), and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`, which owns the exact message. The `read-barrier` fixture proves the denial through the executor in a Loader-booted composition, and the `read-barrier-denied` snapshot pins the model-visible text and the durable record; both are keyless, the snapshot replaying a committed script through `dsh-llm-replay`.
120	3. `ToolAuthority` on `ToolDefinition`, the declarations in `dsh-tool-session-query` and `dsh-tool-cordis`, `role` in `preset.yml`, the `mountPreset` audit, and the per-agent tool guard. Adds the `read-barrier-guard` fixture.
121	4. The certificate invariant: the `recordRun` precondition, the companion's rule, the `read-barrier/attestation` event and its file check, and the `CertificateIsolation` documentation change. The environment runner gains `EnvironmentRunRequest.preset` and refuses a claim above `none` when the resolved preset's role is not `implementer`.
122	5. `deniedReadRoots` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy`, the `dsh-sandbox-local` backends, the `dsh-sandbox-policy` fill from the barrier, the confined ripgrep spawn in `dsh-tool-fs-search`, and the refusals in the workflow engine and the out-of-process subagent providers. This is the slice that makes `process` claimable.
123	6. Tamper: `task.immutable` in `dsh-environments`, the runner's baseline and per-attempt digest over check-owned paths, `verdict` on `verification/run`, the `tamper` reward basis in `dsh-trajectories`, and the `read-barrier-tamper` fixture and snapshot. It follows the `verification/run` event from the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md).
124	7. The blind judge: the shipped `system`-trust judge preset, the lineage-free creation path, the `judge/session` event, and the invariant that rejects a seeded judge. The judging Consumer itself belongs to the oversight seam of the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md).
125	
126	## Risks
127	
128	The barrier is trusted code in the implementer's own process below `host`. A plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit events and reads any path, exactly as `dsh-verification` already states for its durable records. The ladder is honest about this: `none` claims nothing, `process` claims only that the composed executors deny, and `host` is the only level whose evidence comes from outside the process.
129	
130	`process` costs enforcement a deployment may not want. Confining every ripgrep spawn, refusing workflow workers, and refusing out-of-process subagent providers removes capability from implementer sessions that claim it; a deployment that wants those capabilities runs at `none` and keeps a certificate that says so.
131	
132	A check's command line stays observable. The barrier protects the script's content and the fixtures, not the argv a process listing shows, so an environment whose check name or arguments encode the assertion leaks it. Environment authors keep the assertion in the script.
133	
134	The census is only as complete as the composition it was taken from. It is appended before the first request and cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names, which catches a tool added later but not a plugin that reads paths without registering a tool at all.
135	
136	Tamper detection is a digest comparison, so it reports that the check-owned set changed and never who changed it or how. A legitimate build step that rewrites a file inside the immutable set fails the run; environment authors declare the immutable set narrowly, and a false verdict costs one run rather than a wrong certificate.
137	
138	Making `trust` enforcing for one field changes what the roster promises. A deployment that configured a `user` root expecting presets to be ordinary compositions now finds one class of declaration refused there; the refusal is listed as a `broken` reason on the same roster page that offers to delete it.
139

121	  static inject = ['fs']
122	
123	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
124	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
125	    // No schema default: the harness home is resolved in the constructor so the
126	    // stored root is always absolute regardless of how it was supplied.
127	    root: z.string(),
128	    denyRoots: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
129	  })
130	
131	  /** The absolute directory the barrier owns; always the first denied directory. */
132	  readonly root: string
133	
134	  /** Absolute directories denied alongside {@link root} by deployment config. */
135	  private readonly configuredDenyRoots: readonly string[]
136	
137	  /** Registered denied directories, keyed per registration so two registrations of one path both hold. */
138	  private readonly protectedRoots = new Map<object, string>()
139	
140	  /** Reserved run directory per session; holding one is what makes a session the implementer. */
141	  private readonly reservations = new Map<SessionId, string>()
142	
143	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
144	    super(ctx, 'readBarrier')
145	    this.root = absoluteDirectory(config.root ?? dshHomePath('verification'), 'root')
146	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `denyRoots`; the cast records
147	    // that runtime fact. `root` has NO schema default, so its fallback to the
148	    // harness home is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
149	    this.configuredDenyRoots = (config.denyRoots as string[]).map(entry => absoluteDirectory(entry, 'denyRoots entry'))
150	    createOwnerOnlyRoot(this.root)
151	    ctx.on('agent/disposed', ({ agent }) => {
152	      // The role belongs to the live session: a disposed agent can no longer
153	      // read, and keeping its reservation would grow the map for a process
154	      // running many environments.
155	      this.reservations.delete(agent.id)
156	    })
157	  }
158	
159	  /**
160	   * Mint the run directory for one agent's session and record that session as
161	   * the implementer. The validator writes its standard snapshot, one script per
162	   * check, and any held-out fixture there, so the command line the implementer
163	   * can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read.
164	   * Reserving the same session twice returns the same directory.
165	   *
166	   * Synchronous so the role is in force the moment the caller returns: an
167	   * awaited reservation would leave a window in which the session's own reads
168	   * are still unrestricted.
169	   * @param agent - the implementer agent whose session the run belongs to.
170	   * @returns the absolute run directory, created owner-only.
171	   */
172	  reserve(agent: Agent): string {
173	    const existing = this.reservations.get(agent.id)
174	    if (existing !== undefined) return existing
175	    const directory = join(this.root, RUNS_DIR, agent.id)
176	    mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
177	    this.reservations.set(agent.id, directory)
178	    return directory
179	  }
180	
181	  /**
182	   * Deny one more directory for as long as the registration lives, so a plugin
183	   * that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment
184	   * repeating it in configuration.
185	   * @param path - absolute or `~`-prefixed directory to deny.
186	   * @returns the registration's disposer.
187	   */
188	  protect(path: string): () => void {
189	    const directory = absoluteDirectory(path, 'protect path')
190	    const registration = {}
191	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
192	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
193	      this.protectedRoots.set(registration, directory)
194	      return () => { this.protectedRoots.delete(registration) }
195	    }, `read-barrier protected root ${directory}`)
196	  }
197	
198	  /**
199	   * Resolve the complete policy for one capability call. A session holding a
200	   * reservation is the implementer; every other session and every agentless
201	   * call is unrestricted.
202	   * @param request - the calling session, when there is one.
203	   * @returns the role, the barrier root, and every denied directory.
204	   */
205	  resolve(request: ReadBarrierRequest = {}): ReadBarrierPolicy {
206	    const role: ReadBarrierRole = request.session !== undefined && this.reservations.has(request.session.id)
207	      ? 'implementer'
208	      : 'unrestricted'
209	    return {
210	      role,
211	      root: this.root,
212	      denied: [...new Set([this.root, ...this.configuredDenyRoots, ...this.protectedRoots.values()])],
213	    }
214	  }
215	
216	  /**
217	   * Decide whether the policy denies reading one resolved target. Each denied
218	   * directory is canonicalized through the filesystem seam immediately before
219	   * its containment test, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was
220	   * resolved is caught. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied.
221	   * @param policy - the policy {@link resolve} returned for this call.
222	   * @param target - the already-resolved target the caller is about to read.
223	   * @returns true when the read must be refused.
224	   */
225	  async denies(policy: ReadBarrierPolicy, target: FsTarget): Promise<boolean> {
226	    if (policy.role !== 'implementer') return false
227	    for (const denied of policy.denied) {
228	      let directory: FsTarget
229	      try {
230	        directory = await this.ctx.fs.resolve(denied)
231	      } catch {
232	        // A denied directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment
233	        // undecidable, and an undecidable read fails closed.
234	        return true
235	      }
236	      if (this.ctx.fs.contains(directory, target)) return true
237	    }
238	    return false
239	  }
240	
241	  /**
242	   * Append the durable record of one refusal. The barrier owns the write so
243	   * every seam that refuses produces the same evidence.
244	   * @param session - the refused session, whose log receives the record.
245	   * @param policy - the policy that refused, supplying the role and root.
246	   * @param capability - the seam that refused the read.
247	   * @param target - the refused target, supplying the model-facing path.
248	   * @returns the payload exactly as it was appended.
249	   */
250	  recordDenial(
251	    session: Session,
252	    policy: ReadBarrierPolicy,
253	    capability: ReadBarrierCapability,
254	    target: FsTarget,
255	  ): ReadBarrierDenial {
256	    const denial: ReadBarrierDenial = {
257	      version: READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION,
258	      role: policy.role,
259	      capability,
260	      displayPath: target.displayPath,
261	      root: policy.root,
262	    }
263	    session.append('read-barrier/denied', denial)
264	    return denial
265	  }
266	}
267	
268	export default ReadBarrierService

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/** Package-owned durable read-barrier invariants. @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier/invariant */
2	
3	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
4	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
5	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
6	import type { ReadBarrierCapability, ReadBarrierDenial } from './types.ts'
7	import { READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION } from './index.ts'
8	
9	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
10	
11	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
12	export const name = 'read-barrier-invariant'
13	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
14	export const inject = ['invariants']
15	
16	/** Every seam that can refuse a read. */
17	const CAPABILITIES: readonly ReadBarrierCapability[] = ['fs', 'shell', 'subprocess', 'terminal']
18	
19	/**
20	 * The barrier root the first refusal in a session named. One composition owns
21	 * one root, so every later refusal in that session must name the same one.
22	 */
23	const sessionRoot = new WeakMap<object, string>()
24	
25	/** Reject a refusal whose payload is not the record this package writes. */
26	function checkPayload(denial: ReadBarrierDenial, seq: number, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
27	  // Widened: the durable log is a boundary, so a version this build does not
28	  // write can still appear here even though the declared type pins one literal.
29	  const version: number = denial.version
30	  if (version !== READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION) {
31	    fail(`session event ${seq} records a read-barrier/denied of unknown version ${JSON.stringify(version)}`)
32	  }
33	  if (!CAPABILITIES.includes(denial.capability)) {
34	    fail(`session event ${seq} records a read-barrier/denied from unknown capability ${JSON.stringify(denial.capability)}`)
35	  }
36	  if (denial.role !== 'implementer') {
37	    fail(`session event ${seq} records a read-barrier/denied for role ${JSON.stringify(denial.role)}; only an implementer is denied a read`)
38	  }
39	}
40	
41	/** Reject a refusal that names a different barrier root than the session's earlier refusals. */
42	function checkConstantRoot(session: object, root: string, seq: number, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
43	  const first = sessionRoot.get(session)
44	  if (first === undefined) {
45	    sessionRoot.set(session, root)
46	    return
47	  }
48	  if (first !== root) {
49	    fail(`session event ${seq} records a read-barrier/denied under root ${JSON.stringify(root)} after ${JSON.stringify(first)}`)
50	  }
51	}
52	
53	/** Validate the package-owned refusal record and ignore unrelated events. */
54	function validateEvent(session: object, event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
55	  if (event.type !== 'read-barrier/denied') return
56	  checkPayload(event.data, event.seq, fail)
57	  checkConstantRoot(session, event.data.root, event.seq, fail)
58	}
59	
60	/* jscpd:ignore-start -- package companions share replay and dispatch plumbing */
61	/** Install validation for loaded and newly appended refusal records. */
62	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
63	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) {
64	    for (const event of session.events) validateEvent(session, event, fail)
65	  }
66	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
67	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
68	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
69	    validateEvent(session, event, fail)
70	  }, { global: true })
71	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
72	/* jscpd:ignore-end */
73	
74	/**
75	 * Register this package's invariant companion.
76	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
77	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
78	 */
79	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
80	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
81

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The read barrier (`ctx.readBarrier`): the policy home for reads an implementer session must not perform, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. It owns one validator-owned directory tree, mints the per-run directory a validator stocks with what its checks execute, collects the directories other plugins register, resolves one policy per session, and decides containment through the filesystem seam. It denies nothing by itself: each path-opening capability enforces the decision in the operation that opens paths, which is what [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`](../../fs/fs-read-barrier/README.md) does for `ctx.fs`. The [read-barrier Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-read-barrier.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: read-barrier
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
12	  config:
13	    root: ~/.dsh/verification
14	    denyRoots:
15	      - /srv/evaluation/fixtures
16	```
17	
18	| Field | Meaning |
19	|---|---|
20	| `root` (default `<harness home>/verification`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns. Created `0700` at load; an existing directory readable beyond its owner is rejected there, and so is a path that is not absolute after `~` expansion. |
21	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Further absolute or `~`-prefixed directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
22	
23	The denied set for a role is deliberately not a field: which directories an `implementer` may read is a security invariant, not a deployment choice. The service requires `fs`, because containment is decided through that seam rather than by parsing path strings.
24	
25	## Service contract
26	
27	`ctx.readBarrier.reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` owner-only, records that session as the `implementer`, and returns the absolute path; reserving the same session again returns the same directory. It is synchronous so the role is in force the moment the caller returns. A validator writes there what its checks execute — the standard snapshot, one script per check, any held-out fixture — so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. The reservation is dropped when the agent is disposed.
28	
29	`ctx.readBarrier.protect(path)` denies one more directory for as long as the registration lives and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration. Two registrations of one path both hold; the directory leaves the denied set when the last is disposed.
30	
31	`ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`. A session holding a reservation is the `implementer`; every other session and every agentless call is `unrestricted`. `denied` lists the root first, then the configured extras, then each registration, without repeats.
32	
33	`ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)` decides containment for an already-resolved `FsTarget`. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing. For an `implementer`, each denied directory is canonicalized through `ctx.fs.resolve` immediately before `ctx.fs.contains` tests it, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was resolved is caught; a directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment undecidable and the read is denied.
34	
35	`ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, capability, target)` appends the log-only `read-barrier/denied` event — `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, with `capability` naming the seam that refused — and returns the payload it appended. The barrier owns the write so every refusing seam produces the same evidence; the path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the record adds evidence and no new disclosure.
36	
37	The separately published `./invariant` companion rejects a refusal recorded for any role but `implementer`, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a different barrier root than the session's earlier refusals.
38	
39	## Model Experience
40	
41	### Refused reads
42	
43	#### What the model sees
44	
45	Nothing this package renders. Its decision reaches the model only as the refusal the enforcing capability returns from the operation the model called: for `ctx.fs` reads that is [`dsh-fs-read-barrier`](../../fs/fs-read-barrier/README.md), which owns the exact message. No prompt section, tool schema, or tool description mentions the barrier, and a session that never reads a denied path cannot tell it is composed.
46	
47	#### Token effect
48	
49	Zero direct tokens. A refused read replaces the tool result the model would have received with the enforcing capability's short error, so a denial spends fewer tokens than the read it refused.
50	
51	#### KV Cache effect
52	
53	Append-only, and prefix-stable: the barrier adds nothing to the system prompt or to tool schemas, and its own event is log-only, so an existing reusable request prefix survives every refusal.
54	
55	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
56	
57	- **The role comes from a reservation only** — a session is the `implementer` because a validator reserved its run directory; a preset cannot declare `implementer` or `validator` for itself yet, so `validator` and `unrestricted` are indistinguishable at the deny decision (both are denied nothing).
58	- **Nothing enforces beyond `ctx.fs`** — `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, and out-of-process subagent and workflow executors open paths this service does not fence, so a composed bash tool still reads the barrier root. The `ReadBarrierCapability` vocabulary names those seams; only `fs` decides today.
59	- **No isolation claim reads this policy** — `dsh-verification` still records the isolation level its caller passes, and no certificate precondition consults the barrier or the refusals it recorded.
60	- **Trusted code in the implementer's own process** — a plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit refusals and reads any path. The barrier confines the composed executors, not the process.
61	- **Owner-only modes stop other accounts, not the model** — the `0700` root is protection against another operating-system user; the harness process runs as the same user as its tools, so the barrier, not the mode, is what denies the model.

119	/**
120	 * Light last-wins fold of the `verification` projection unit. Unlike the
121	 * strict replay fold (fold.ts: transition validation, fail-loud on malformed
122	 * changes), this transition is projection-grade: the state is plain JSON, any
123	 * non-verification or malformed event returns the same reference, and
124	 * correctness of the written change is the write side's job.
125	 * @param state - the projection covering all prior events.
126	 * @param event - the next committed session event.
127	 * @returns the next projection (same reference when the event is not a well-formed verification change).
128	 */
129	export function applyVerificationProjection(
130	  state: VerificationProjection | null,
131	  event: SessionEvent,
132	): VerificationProjection | null {
133	  try {
134	    switch (event.type) {
135	      case 'verification/standard': {
136	        const change = decodeStandardChange(event.data)
137	        if (change === undefined) return state
138	        return {
139	          standard: change.standard,
140	          directivesIssued: state?.directivesIssued ?? 0,
141	          runsRecorded: state?.runsRecorded ?? 0,
142	          createdAt: change.createdAt,
143	          updatedAt: change.updatedAt,
144	        }
145	      }
146	      case 'verification/relaxation': {
147	        const change = decodeRelaxationChange(event.data)
148	        if (change === undefined) return state
149	        return {
150	          standard: change.standard,
151	          directivesIssued: state?.directivesIssued ?? 0,
152	          runsRecorded: state?.runsRecorded ?? 0,
153	          createdAt: change.createdAt,
154	          updatedAt: change.updatedAt,
155	        }
156	      }
157	      case 'verification/run': {
158	        const change = decodeRunChange(event.data)
159	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
160	        return { ...state, runsRecorded: state.runsRecorded + 1 }
161	      }
162	      case 'verification/certificate': {
163	        const change = decodeCertificateChange(event.data)
164	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
165	        return { ...state, certificate: change.certificate }
166	      }
167	      case 'verification/directive': {
168	        const change = decodeDirectiveChange(event.data)
169	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
170	        return { ...state, directivesIssued: state.directivesIssued + 1 }
171	      }
172	      default:
173	        return state
174	    }
175	  } catch (_invalidPersistedVerificationChange) {
176	    return state
177	  }
178	}

203	function resolveBound(value: number, field: string): number {
204	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value < 1) {

210	/** Completion-standard service (`ctx.completionStandards`) backed exclusively by the owning session log. */
211	export class CompletionStandardService extends Service {
212	  static inject = ['agents']
213	
214	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
215	    maxChecks: z.number().default(256),
216	    maxTextChars: z.number().default(16384),
217	  })
218	
219	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
220	  private readonly caches = new WeakMap<Session, VerificationCache>()
221	
222	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
223	    super(ctx, 'completionStandards')
224	    this.resolved = {
225	      maxChecks: resolveBound(config.maxChecks ?? 256, 'maxChecks'),
226	      maxTextChars: resolveBound(config.maxTextChars ?? 16384, 'maxTextChars'),
227	    }
228	    // Certificate admission activates only when a goal service is composed
229	    // (assemblies without goals keep the service verbs alone).
230	    ctx.inject(['goals'], (goalsCtx) => {
231	      goalsCtx.effect(() => goalsCtx.goals.completionGuard((agent, goal) => {
232	        this.guardCompletion(agent, goal.id)
233	      }))
234	    })
235	    // The `verification` projection unit: last-wins fold of the five
236	    // verification events (see applyVerificationProjection). The unit child
237	    // activates only when a projection registry is composed.
238	    ctx.inject(['sessionProjections'], (projectionCtx) => {
239	      projectionCtx.sessionProjections.register<'verification', VerificationProjection | null>({
240	        key: 'verification',
241	        schema: verificationProjectionSchema,
242	        init: () => null,
243	        apply: applyVerificationProjection,
244	        view: state => state,
245	        stateVersion: 2,
246	      })
247	    })
248	  }

250	  /**
251	   * Read the current standard for one exact live agent.
252	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
253	   * @returns a fresh view or `undefined` when no standard is current.
254	   * @throws {@link VerificationError} when the agent is not the registry's live instance.
255	   */
256	  get(agent: Agent): StandardView | undefined {
257	    this.assertLive(agent)
258	    const cache = this.cache(agent.session)
259	    this.sync(agent.session, cache)
260	    return this.view(cache)
261	  }
262	
263	  /**
264	   * Author the executable standard for one goal before implementation begins.
265	   * A current standard for a different goal is superseded; authoring twice
266	   * for the same goal is rejected — grow it with {@link extend} instead.
267	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
268	   * @param request - goal identity and the initial non-empty check inventory.
269	   * @returns the authored view at revision one.
270	   */
271	  author(agent: Agent, request: AuthorStandardRequest): StandardView {
272	    const checks = this.resolveChecks(request.checks, new Set())
273	    if (checks.length === 0) {
274	      throw new VerificationError('standard requires at least one check', 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')
275	    }
276	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
277	    const current = cache.state.standard
278	    if (current !== undefined && current.goalId === request.goalId) {
279	      throw new VerificationError(
280	        `standard "${current.id}" already measures goal "${current.goalId}"`,
281	        'VERIFICATION_STANDARD_EXISTS',
282	      )
283	    }
284	    const now = Date.now()
285	    const standard: CompletionStandardSnapshot = {
286	      id: StandardId(`standard-${randomUUID()}`),
287	      revision: 1,
288	      goalId: request.goalId,
289	      checks,
290	      relaxed: [],
291	    }
292	    return this.commitStandard(agent, cache, 'author', standard, now, now)
293	  }
294	
295	  /**
296	   * Add checks to the current standard. Existing checks and relaxations are
297	   * preserved exactly; the mutation invalidates any prior certificate.
298	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
299	   * @param ref - expected current revision.
300	   * @param checks - one or more checks to append.
301	   * @returns the extended view.
302	   */
303	  extend(agent: Agent, ref: StandardRef, checks: readonly StandardCheck[]): StandardView {
304	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
305	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)
306	    const taken = new Set<string>([
307	      ...current.checks.map(check => check.id),
308	      ...current.relaxed.map(entry => entry.check.id),
309	    ])
310	    const added = this.resolveChecks(checks, taken)
311	    if (added.length === 0) {
312	      throw new VerificationError('extend requires at least one added check', 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')
313	    }
314	    const standard: CompletionStandardSnapshot = {
315	      ...current,
316	      revision: current.revision + 1,
317	      checks: [...current.checks, ...added],
318	    }
319	    if (standard.checks.length > this.resolved.maxChecks) {
320	      throw new VerificationError(
321	        `standard cannot exceed ${this.resolved.maxChecks} active checks`,
322	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK',
323	      )
324	    }
325	    return this.commitStandard(agent, cache, 'extend', standard, this.currentCreatedAt(cache), this.nextMutationTime(cache))
326	  }
327	
328	  /**
329	   * Remove one check with recorded evidence that its stricter form is
330	   * unsatisfiable. The mutation invalidates any prior certificate.
331	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
332	   * @param ref - expected current revision.
333	   * @param checkId - active check to relax.
334	   * @param evidence - non-empty unsatisfiability evidence.
335	   * @returns the relaxed view.
336	   */
337	  relax(agent: Agent, ref: StandardRef, checkId: CheckId, evidence: string): StandardView {
338	    const recorded = this.text(evidence, 'evidence', 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RELAXATION')
339	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
340	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)
341	    const removed = current.checks.find(check => check.id === checkId)
342	    if (removed === undefined) {
343	      throw new VerificationError(
344	        `standard "${current.id}" has no active check "${checkId}"`,
345	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RELAXATION',
346	      )
347	    }
348	    const standard: CompletionStandardSnapshot = {
349	      ...current,
350	      revision: current.revision + 1,
351	      checks: current.checks.filter(check => check.id !== checkId),
352	      relaxed: [...current.relaxed, { check: removed, evidence: recorded }],
353	    }
354	    const change: RelaxationChangeMeta = {
355	      kind: 'verification/relaxation',
356	      version: VERIFICATION_CHANGE_VERSION,
357	      checkId,
358	      standard,
359	      createdAt: this.currentCreatedAt(cache),
360	      updatedAt: this.nextMutationTime(cache),
361	    }
362	    this.commit(agent, cache, 'verification/relaxation', change)
363	    return this.currentView(cache)
364	  }

366	  /**
367	   * Record one complete run of the current standard. Every run appends a
368	   * durable `verification/run` event carrying all of its results; a fully
369	   * passing run then commits a certificate, while any failure returns the
370	   * failing subset the validator aggregates into a {@link issueDirective}
371	   * directive.
372	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
373	   * @param ref - expected current revision.
374	   * @param isolation - isolation level the run executed under.
375	   * @param results - exactly one result per active check, any order.
376	   * @param evidence - executor of the checks and the workspace digest it covered.
377	   * @returns the certificate, or the failing results.
378	   */
379	  recordRun(
380	    agent: Agent,
381	    ref: StandardRef,
382	    isolation: CertificateIsolation,
383	    results: readonly CheckResult[],
384	    evidence: RunEvidence,
385	  ): RunOutcome {
386	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
387	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)
388	    const byCheck = new Map<string, CheckResult>()
389	    for (const result of results) {
390	      if (byCheck.has(result.checkId)) {
391	        throw new VerificationError(`duplicate result for check "${result.checkId}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS')
392	      }
393	      byCheck.set(result.checkId, {
394	        checkId: result.checkId,
395	        status: result.status,
396	        evidence: this.text(result.evidence, `result for "${result.checkId}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS'),
397	      })
398	    }
399	    const ordered: CheckResult[] = []
400	    for (const check of current.checks) {
401	      const result = byCheck.get(check.id)
402	      if (result === undefined) {
403	        throw new VerificationError(`run is missing a result for check "${check.id}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS')
404	      }
405	      byCheck.delete(check.id)
406	      ordered.push(result)
407	    }
408	    const extra = [...byCheck.keys()]
409	    if (extra.length > 0) {
410	      throw new VerificationError(
411	        `run answers unknown check(s) ${extra.map(id => `"${id}"`).join(', ')}`,
412	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS',
413	      )
414	    }
415	    const standard: StandardRef = { id: current.id, revision: current.revision }
416	    const run: VerificationRunChangeMeta = {
417	      kind: 'verification/run',
418	      version: VERIFICATION_CHANGE_VERSION,
419	      standard,

3	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
4	import { decodeGoalChange } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
5	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
6	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
7	import { applyVerificationEvent, decodeCertificateChange, emptyVerificationFoldState } from './fold.ts'
8	import type { VerificationFoldState } from './fold.ts'
9	import type { CertificateChangeMeta } from './domain.ts'
10	
11	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
12	
13	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
14	export const name = 'verification-invariant'
15	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
16	export const inject = ['invariants']
17	
18	/** Copy the independent fold before validating one candidate event. */
19	function cloneState(state: VerificationFoldState): VerificationFoldState {
20	  return {
21	    standard: state.standard,
22	    certificate: state.certificate,
23	    directivesIssued: state.directivesIssued,
24	    runsRecorded: state.runsRecorded,
25	    lastRun: state.lastRun,
26	    createdAt: state.createdAt,
27	    updatedAt: state.updatedAt,
28	    lastRef: state.lastRef,
29	    seenStandardIds: new Set(state.seenStandardIds),
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Decode a certificate for a relation check, leaving malformed payloads to the strict fold. */
34	function certificateOf(event: SessionEvent): CertificateChangeMeta | undefined {
35	  try {
36	    return decodeCertificateChange(event.data)
37	  } catch (_malformedCertificateChange) {
38	    // A malformed certificate is applyChecked's own subject: the strict fold rejects it.
39	    return undefined
40	  }
41	}
42	
43	/** Reject a certificate that no fully passing run of the same standard revision preceded. */
44	function checkCertifiedRunExecuted(state: VerificationFoldState, event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
45	  if (event.type !== 'verification/certificate') return
46	  const change = certificateOf(event)
47	  if (change === undefined) return
48	  const covered = change.certificate.standard
49	  const run = state.lastRun
50	  if (run !== undefined && run.standard.id === covered.id && run.standard.revision === covered.revision
51	    && run.results.every(result => result.status === 'pass')) {
52	    return
53	  }
54	  fail(`session event ${event.seq} certifies standard "${covered.id}" revision ${covered.revision} without a preceding fully passing verification/run`)
55	}
56	
57	/** Reject a goal completion that a current standard measures without a covering certificate. */
58	function checkGoalCompletion(state: VerificationFoldState, event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
59	  if (event.type !== 'goal/change') return
60	  let completedGoalId: string | undefined
61	  try {
62	    const change = decodeGoalChange(event.data)
63	    if (change === undefined || change.operation !== 'complete') return
64	    completedGoalId = change.goal.id
65	  } catch (_malformedGoalChange) {
66	    // Malformed goal changes are the dsh-goal invariant companion's subject.
67	    return
68	  }
69	  const standard = state.standard
70	  if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== completedGoalId) return
71	  if (state.certificate === undefined) {
72	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} completes goal "${completedGoalId}" while standard "${standard.id}" revision ${standard.revision} has no covering certificate`)
73	  }
74	}
75	
76	/** Apply one event through the strict verification decoder and attribute failures. */
77	function applyChecked(state: VerificationFoldState, event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
78	  checkGoalCompletion(state, event, fail)
79	  checkCertifiedRunExecuted(state, event, fail)
80	  try {
81	    applyVerificationEvent(state, event)
82	  } catch (error) {
83	    /* v8 ignore next -- the strict verification decoder throws Error instances */
84	    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
85	    fail(`session event ${event.seq} violates the durable verification stream: ${message}`)
86	  }
87	}
88	
89	/** Install an independent incremental fold over every attached session. */
90	// The staged session-fold scaffold deliberately mirrors every sibling companion (goal is the template).
91	/* jscpd:ignore-start */
92	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
93	  const states = new WeakMap<Session, VerificationFoldState>()
94	  const staged = new WeakMap<SessionEvent, { session: Session; state: VerificationFoldState }>()
95	
96	  const seed = (session: Session): VerificationFoldState => {
97	    const state = emptyVerificationFoldState()
98	    for (const event of session.events) applyChecked(state, event, fail)
99	    states.set(session, state)
100	    return state
101	  }
102	  /* v8 ignore next -- session/event always follows list() or session/created seeding */
103	  const stateFor = (session: Session): VerificationFoldState => states.get(session) ?? seed(session)
104	
105	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) seed(session)
106	  ctx.on('session/created', (session) => { seed(session) }, { global: true })
107	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
108	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
109	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
110	    const state = cloneState(stateFor(session))
111	    applyChecked(state, event, fail)
112	    staged.set(event, { session, state })
113	  }, { global: true })
114	  ctx.on('session/event', (session, event) => {
115	    const candidate = staged.get(event)
116	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- internal/dispatch stages the exact callback arguments */
117	    if (candidate === undefined || candidate.session !== session) {
118	      return fail('session/event reached publication without matching verification-fold validation')
119	    }
120	    staged.delete(event)
121	    states.set(session, candidate.state)
122	  }, { global: true })
123	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
124	/* jscpd:ignore-end */
125	
126	/**
127	 * Register the verification-stream invariant companion.
128	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
129	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
130	 */
131	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
132	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))

1	/**
2	 * A preset's display metadata: the name and description a picker shows.
3	 *
4	 * It lives in its own file because the composition is a top-level list of
5	 * plugin rows — YAML cannot carry sibling keys beside it, and faking a
6	 * metadata row would hand the Loader something to load. Keeping it separate
7	 * also keeps the composition exactly what its name says: a Cordis file the
8	 * loader owns and the cordis preset can author.
9	 *
10	 * The file carries display text ONLY. `id` is the directory name and `trust`
11	 * comes from the root a preset was discovered under, so neither is writable
12	 * here — otherwise a locally authored preset could claim to be a shipped one.
13	 *
14	 * Every read failure degrades to no metadata. A preset whose display text is
15	 * missing, malformed, or unreadable still mounts: presentation is not a
16	 * capability, and a broken name must never become an agent that cannot start.
17	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/metadata
18	 */
19	
20	import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
21	import { join } from 'node:path'
22	import yaml from 'js-yaml'
23	
24	/** The optional display-metadata file beside a preset's composition. */
25	export const METADATA_FILE = 'preset.yml'
26	
27	/** Display text a preset may publish about itself. */
28	export interface PresetMetadata {
29	  /** Human-facing name; falls back to the preset id when absent. */
30	  readonly name?: string
31	  /** One sentence on what this preset is for. */
32	  readonly description?: string
33	  /**
34	   * Position within its group; lower comes first. A preset that declares
35	   * none sorts after every preset that does, then by id — so the shipped set
36	   * can read in capability order while authored ones stay alphabetical.
37	   */
38	  readonly order?: number
39	}
40	
41	/** A non-empty trimmed string, or undefined for anything else. */
42	function text(value: unknown): string | undefined {
43	  if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined
44	  const trimmed = value.trim()
45	  return trimmed === '' ? undefined : trimmed
46	}
47	
48	/**
49	 * Read one preset directory's display metadata.
50	 *
51	 * Absent, unparsable, and wrongly-shaped files are all the same answer —
52	 * empty metadata — because the caller renders a picker, not a diagnostic.
53	 * @param directory - the preset directory.
54	 * @returns the display text the preset published, possibly empty.
55	 */
56	export async function readPresetMetadata(directory: string): Promise<PresetMetadata> {
57	  let raw: string
58	  try {
59	    raw = await readFile(join(directory, METADATA_FILE), 'utf8')
60	  } catch {
61	    // Absent is the common case: metadata is optional and most presets,
62	    // including every one authored by duplicating another, carry none.
63	    return {}
64	  }
65	  let parsed: unknown
66	  try {
67	    parsed = yaml.load(raw)
68	  } catch {
69	    // Malformed display text is not worth failing discovery over; the picker
70	    // falls back to the id, and the composition still mounts.
71	    return {}
72	  }
73	  if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) return {}
74	  const record = parsed as Record<string, unknown>
75	  const name = text(record.name)
76	  const description = text(record.description)
77	  const order = typeof record.order === 'number' && Number.isFinite(record.order)
78	    ? record.order
79	    : undefined
80	  return {
81	    ...name === undefined ? {} : { name },
82	    ...description === undefined ? {} : { description },
83	    ...order === undefined ? {} : { order },
84	  }
85	}
86	
87	/**
88	 * Render display metadata as the file's contents.
89	 *
90	 * Absent fields are omitted rather than written empty, so a preset with no
91	 * description does not ship a key that reads as an intentional blank.
92	 * @param metadata - the display text to store.
93	 * @returns the YAML document, or undefined when there is nothing to store.
94	 */
95	export function renderPresetMetadata(metadata: PresetMetadata): string | undefined {
96	  const name = text(metadata.name)
97	  const description = text(metadata.description)
98	  const { order } = metadata
99	  if (name === undefined && description === undefined && order === undefined) return undefined
100	  return yaml.dump({
101	    ...name === undefined ? {} : { name },
102	    ...description === undefined ? {} : { description },
103	    ...order === undefined ? {} : { order },
104	  }, { lineWidth: -1 })
105	}

1	/**
2	 * Mount one preset composition under an agent's scope context, then prove the
3	 * result is usable before the agent is published.
4	 *
5	 * The scope context is what makes the composition per-session: entry contexts
6	 * chain to the context the subtree was plugged into, so every `ctx.tools`
7	 * and `ctx.systemPrompt` registration inside the preset files into that
8	 * agent's layer and unwinds with it. Two guards make that safe. A row that
9	 * never reached a usable state is rejected, because a directly-plugged subtree
10	 * is absent from `ctx.loader.entries()` and no boot audit covers it. A row that
11	 * published a service into the ROOT realm is rejected, because such a service
12	 * is process-global rather than per-session and the second session mounting the
13	 * same preset collides with the first.
14	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/mount
15	 */
16	
17	import { isAbsolute } from 'node:path'
18	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
19	import { Context, type Fiber } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
20	import { Include } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
21	import type { EntryTree } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
22	import { scopeOf, scopeParentOf, type ScopeKey } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
23	import { PresetMountError, type AgentPreset } from './preset.ts'
