25	/** What one mounted subtree publishes about itself for the audit to read. */
26	interface MountedTree {
27	  /** The rows the composition created. */
28	  readonly tree: EntryTree
29	  /**
30	   * The subtree's own fiber. Captured here rather than taken from
31	   * `ctx.plugin()`, which hands back a thenable `Object.create(fiber)` wrapper
32	   * that is never identical to the fiber appearing in a parent chain.
33	   */
34	  readonly fiber: Fiber
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * Subtrees captured by config identity. A subtree plugged directly (rather than
39	 * created as a loader entry) never links itself to an `Entry`, so this is the
40	 * only handle to the rows it created; config objects are minted per mount, so
41	 * concurrent mounts cannot collide.
42	 */
43	const mounted = new WeakMap<object, MountedTree>()
44	
45	/**
46	 * The base URL bare specifiers resolve against, per pending mount, keyed by the
47	 * same config object. Recorded before the subtree is plugged, because `Include`
48	 * rewrites its own context's `baseUrl` to the composition's directory and the
49	 * pre-mount value is the only handle on where the harness itself lives.
50	 */
51	const harnessBase = new WeakMap<object, string>()
52	
53	/**
54	 * Include subclass that publishes its tree and fiber for the audit, and never
55	 * writes to the file it read.
56	 */
57	class PresetTree extends Include {
58	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Include.Config) {
59	    super(ctx, config)
60	    mounted.set(config, { tree: this, fiber: ctx.fiber })
61	  }
62	
63	  /**
64	   * Resolve a bare specifier from the harness rather than from the preset.
65	   *
66	   * `EntryTree.import()` resolves against the tree's own `baseUrl`, which
67	   * `Include` sets to the composition's directory. That is right for a
68	   * relative specifier — a preset's own files travel with it — and wrong for
69	   * a package name: a locally authored preset lives under the user's home,
70	   * where Node's upward `node_modules` walk never reaches the harness's own
71	   * dependencies, so every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` row would fail to import. The
72	   * mount records the host composition's base instead, which is inside the
73	   * installed harness, and bare names resolve from there. An absolute
74	   * filesystem path names neither base and becomes a file URL before Node's
75	   * ESM loader receives it, which is required for drive-letter paths on
76	   * Windows.
77	   * @param name - the module specifier from the row.
78	   * @param getOuterStack - the loader's stack composer for import diagnostics.
79	   * @returns the imported module, or the `cordis:` builtin.
80	   */
81	  override import(name: string, getOuterStack?: () => string[]): unknown {
82	    const specifier = isAbsolute(name) ? pathToFileURL(name).href : name
83	    const base = harnessBase.get(this.config)
84	    /* v8 ignore next -- every PresetTree is constructed by `mountPreset`, which records the base first */
85	    if (base === undefined) return super.import(specifier, getOuterStack)
86	    if (name.startsWith('.') || name.startsWith('cordis:')) return super.import(name, getOuterStack)
87	    const internal = this.ctx.loader.internal
88	    /* v8 ignore next -- Node always supplies the internal module loader; the branch keeps a
89	       hypothetical embedder from losing the row's name in a resolution error. */
90	    if (internal === undefined) return super.import(specifier, getOuterStack)
91	    return internal.import(specifier, base, {})
92	  }
93	
94	  /**
95	   * A preset is an input, never a persistence target.
96	   *
97	   * The Loader writes a tree back through this method whenever it decides the
98	   * config changed — a plugin self-disposing is enough, and tearing an agent
99	   * down disposes its whole subtree. Inherited, that rewrites the preset file
100	   * with whatever the dying tree held, which in practice means truncating a
101	   * shipped composition to `[]` the first time a session ends. Persisting a
102	   * preset is also meaningless: nothing here is user state, and the same file
103	   * backs every session that names it.
104	   *
105	   * Dropping the write drops the `loader/config-update` the inherited method
106	   * emits with it. Nothing observes one for a preset subtree today, and a
107	   * future "edit your preset while it runs" flow needs a deliberate
108	   * persistence path rather than this method's return.
109	   */
110	  override write(): void {
111	  }
112	}

114	/** One preset composition currently installed under some agent. */
115	export interface PresetMount {
116	  /** The preset the subtree was composed from. */
117	  readonly presetId: string
118	  /** The mounted subtree's fiber. */
119	  readonly fiber: Fiber
120	  /** The standing scope key agents are parented to (undefined only in torn-down records). */
121	  readonly key: ScopeKey | undefined
122	}
123	
124	const mounts = new Set<PresetMount>()
125	
126	/**
127	 * Drop every record whose subtree is gone.
128	 *
129	 * Records are pruned by observation rather than through a disposal hook
130	 * because a subtree can be torn down by its owning agent, by a failed mount, or
131	 * by the whole tree unloading, and a cleared `uid` is what all three share.
132	 *
133	 * Pruning therefore has to happen on a path this module owns. Reading is one
134	 * such path, but not a reliable one: the only production reader is the
135	 * invariant companion's service listener, and `dsh-invariants` is a
136	 * development composition — a shipped host never loads it. Mounting is the
137	 * other, and it is the one every session takes, which bounds the set at one
138	 * generation of dead records rather than one per session ever composed. Each
139	 * record would otherwise retain its whole disposed subtree: the fiber holds
140	 * its config, and that config is the key its `EntryTree` is stored under.
141	 */
142	function pruneDisposedMounts(): void {
143	  for (const mount of mounts) {
144	    if (mount.fiber.uid === null) mounts.delete(mount)
145	  }
146	}
147	
148	/**
149	 * Every preset composition still installed, pruning fibers disposed since the
150	 * last read.
151	 * @returns the live mounts.
152	 */
153	export function livePresetMounts(): PresetMount[] {
154	  pruneDisposedMounts()
155	  return [...mounts]
156	}

158	/**
159	 * Whether `fiber` is `root` itself or is mounted anywhere inside its subtree.
160	 *
161	 * Membership is object identity. `uid` looks like a cheaper key but is a
162	 * per-registry counter, so fibers in two different roots collide on it and a
163	 * subtree in one runtime would be blamed for a service published in another.
164	 * @param fiber - the fiber to locate.
165	 * @param root - the subtree root to test membership against.
166	 * @returns true when `fiber` belongs to `root`'s subtree.
167	 */
168	function withinFiber(fiber: Fiber, root: Fiber): boolean {
169	  let current = fiber
170	  while (true) {
171	    if (current === root) return true
172	    const parent = current.parent.fiber
173	    if (parent === current) return false
174	    current = parent
175	  }
176	}

178	/**
179	 * Service names the mounted subtree published into the root realm.
180	 *
181	 * A provider without an `isolate` realm stores its implementation under the
182	 * root's symbol for that name, which is exactly the comparison below; a
183	 * provider inside an `isolate` realm stores under a realm-private symbol and
184	 * is correctly absent here.
185	 * @param ctx - any context of the runtime whose service store is inspected.
186	 * @param mount - the mounted subtree's fiber.
187	 * @returns the leaked service names in lexical order.
188	 */
189	export function leakedServices(ctx: Context, mount: Fiber): string[] {
190	  const store = ctx.reflect.store
191	  const rootIsolate = ctx.root[Context.isolate]
192	  const leaked: string[] = []
193	  for (const key of Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(store)) {
194	    const impl = store[key]
195	    /* v8 ignore next -- cordis deletes a store slot on disposal rather than
196	       clearing it, so an own symbol always resolves; the guard exists only
197	       because the store's index signature is optional. */
198	    if (impl === undefined) continue
199	    if (!withinFiber(impl.fiber, mount)) continue
200	    if (rootIsolate[impl.name] === key) leaked.push(impl.name)
201	  }
202	  return leaked.sort((left, right) => left.localeCompare(right))
203	}

205	/** A live standing mount located through one agent already joined to it. */
206	export type JoinedPresetMount = PresetMount & {
207	  /** The standing key, definite because it is what the lookup matched on. */
208	  readonly key: ScopeKey
209	}
210	
211	/**
212	 * The standing composition one agent is joined to.
213	 *
214	 * The agent's own key is parented to its preset's standing key, so the mount
215	 * is found by matching that parent rather than by walking up from the agent —
216	 * the mount is not under the agent's fiber. An agent that joined no preset —
217	 * a deployment composing no roster, or a child agent before its join — has no
218	 * parent link and resolves to undefined.
219	 * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context.
220	 * @returns the mount the agent joined, or undefined when it joined none.
221	 */
222	export function standingMountFor(agentCtx: Context): JoinedPresetMount | undefined {
223	  const agentKey = scopeOf(agentCtx)
224	  if (agentKey === undefined) return undefined
225	  const standingKey = scopeParentOf(agentKey)
226	  if (standingKey === undefined) return undefined
227	  return livePresetMounts().find(
228	    (candidate): candidate is JoinedPresetMount => candidate.key === standingKey,
229	  )
230	}

232	/**
233	 * One agent's instance of a service its preset mounted.
234	 *
235	 * A preset publishes a service behind an `isolate` realm so two sessions
236	 * cannot collide, and an entry-local realm is invisible to everything outside
237	 * the group — including the agent's own scope context and the host. That is
238	 * right for the rows inside the group and wrong for one caller: a request that
239	 * is ABOUT a session but arrives from outside it, which is every browser RPC
240	 * the api-proxy serves.
241	 *
242	 * Ownership is the same relation {@link leakedServices} reads, inverted: there
243	 * it names implementations a subtree published into the ROOT realm, here it
244	 * names the one this subtree published anywhere. Fiber membership is object
245	 * identity for the reason stated on {@link withinFiber}.
246	 *
247	 * This is READ addressing for a caller that already holds the agent. It is not
248	 * a general host handle on a session's internals: a host row that `inject`s a
249	 * service cannot use it, because injection resolves before any session exists
250	 * and has no agent to key by — such a service belongs on the host plane.
251	 * @param ctx - any context of the runtime whose service store is inspected.
252	 * @param agent - the agent whose mounted composition to look inside.
253	 * @param name - the service name as the preset's rows resolve it.
254	 * @returns the agent's instance, or undefined when its preset mounts none.
255	 */
256	export function serviceForAgent<K extends string & keyof Context>(
257	  ctx: Context,
258	  agent: { ctx: Context },
259	  name: K,
260	): Context[K] | undefined {
261	  const mount = standingMountFor(agent.ctx)
262	  if (mount === undefined) return undefined
263	  const store = ctx.reflect.store
264	  for (const key of Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(store)) {
265	    const impl = store[key]
266	    /* v8 ignore next -- cordis deletes a store slot on disposal rather than clearing it */
267	    if (impl === undefined) continue
268	    if (impl.name !== name) continue
269	    if (withinFiber(impl.fiber, mount.fiber)) return impl.value as Context[K]
270	  }
271	  return undefined
272	}

274	/**
275	 * Rows that did not reach a usable state, each rendered as one diagnostic line.
276	 *
277	 * A row whose module failed to import or whose plugin threw already rejects the
278	 * mount through the loader; what remains observable here is a row still waiting
279	 * for a service the composition never supplies.
280	 * @param tree - the mounted subtree.
281	 * @returns one line per unusable row, empty when every enabled row is usable.
282	 */
283	export function inactiveRows(tree: EntryTree): string[] {
284	  const lines: string[] = []
285	  for (const entry of tree.entries()) {
286	    if (entry.disabled) continue
287	    const fiber = entry.fiber
288	    /* v8 ignore next 4 -- the loader rejects an entry whose module or plugin failed,
289	       so a settled tree never holds an enabled fiber-less entry; the branch exists
290	       only because `Entry.fiber` is declared optional. */
291	    if (fiber === undefined) {
292	      lines.push(`${entry.options.id} (${entry.options.name}): never started`)
293	      continue
294	    }
295	    const missing = Object.keys(fiber.inject).filter(name => fiber.ctx.get(name) === undefined)
296	    if (missing.length > 0) {
297	      lines.push(`${entry.options.id} (${entry.options.name}): waiting for ${missing.join(', ')}`)
298	    }
299	  }
300	  return lines
301	}

303	/**
304	 * The reportable text of a mount failure.
305	 *
306	 * The loader reports several failed rows as one `AggregateError`, whose own
307	 * message names none of them; without flattening, a composition that fails on
308	 * two rows says only "loader entries failed to apply" and the operator has
309	 * nothing to act on.
310	 * @param error - the value the mount rejected with.
311	 * @returns a single-line-per-cause description.
312	 */
313	function mountDetail(error: unknown): string {
314	  /* v8 ignore next -- every path into the mount's catch throws an Error: the loader
315	     wraps a row's thrown value before it propagates, and this module's own
316	     rejections are Errors. The fallback keeps a hostile value readable. */
317	  if (!(error instanceof Error)) return String(error)
318	  if (!(error instanceof AggregateError)) return error.message
319	  return [error.message, ...error.errors.map(cause => `- ${mountDetail(cause)}`)].join('\n')
320	}

322	/**
323	 * Mount `preset` under `agentCtx` and return only once every row is usable.
324	 *
325	 * The subtree is owned by `agentCtx`'s fiber, so it unwinds with the agent and
326	 * the caller receives no disposer. A rejection leaves nothing mounted.
327	 * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context, from the agent factory's `setup`.
328	 * @param preset - the resolved preset to compose the agent from.
329	 * @throws when `agentCtx` carries no scope, a row is unusable, or a row
330	 * published a service into the root realm.
331	 */
332	export async function mountPreset(agentCtx: Context, preset: AgentPreset): Promise<void> {
333	  const scope = scopeOf(agentCtx)
334	  if (scope === undefined) {
335	    throw new Error(
336	      `agent-presets: refusing to mount preset "${preset.id}" into an unscoped context; `
337	      + 'its registrations would apply to every agent in the process',
338	    )
339	  }
340	  const config: Include.Config = { path: pathToFileURL(preset.path).href }
341	  // Captured before the subtree exists: the standing scope context still
342	  // carries the host composition's base, which is inside the installed
343	  // harness and is therefore where a row's package name has to resolve from.
344	  /* v8 ignore next -- the Loader sets `baseUrl` on the root before any scoped context derives from it */
345	  if (agentCtx.baseUrl !== undefined) harnessBase.set(config, agentCtx.baseUrl)
346	  // Before the record this mount is about to add: standing mounts are one per
347	  // preset and live until whole-tree teardown, so pruning here only sweeps
348	  // records of torn-down runtimes (tests; an HMR reload of the roster).
349	  pruneDisposedMounts()
350	  const handle = agentCtx.plugin(PresetTree, config)
351	  try {
352	    await handle.await()
353	    const subtree = mounted.get(config)
354	    /* v8 ignore next -- the subclass constructor runs before `await()` settles for every mounted tree */
355	    if (subtree === undefined) throw new Error('mounted subtree did not publish its entry tree')
356	    const { tree, fiber } = subtree
357	    const unusable = inactiveRows(tree)
358	    if (unusable.length > 0) {
359	      throw new Error(`${String(unusable.length)} row(s) did not activate:\n${unusable.join('\n')}`)
360	    }
361	    const leaked = leakedServices(agentCtx, fiber)
362	    if (leaked.length > 0) {
363	      throw new Error(
364	        `row(s) published process-global service(s) [${leaked.join(', ')}]; `
365	        + 'a preset service must sit behind an `isolate` realm or move to the host composition',
366	      )
367	    }
368	    mounts.add({ presetId: preset.id, fiber, key: scopeOf(agentCtx) })
369	  } catch (error) {
370	    try {
371	      await handle.dispose()
372	    /* v8 ignore next 5 -- teardown of a subtree nothing else references has no
373	       observed failure mode; the guard exists so a teardown error cannot
374	       replace the mount diagnostic the caller needs. */
375	    } catch {
376	      // Swallows only this subtree's teardown failure. The mount error below is
377	      // the actionable one, and the discarded fiber is unreachable either way.
378	    }
379	    throw new PresetMountError(preset.id, `${mountDetail(error)} (${preset.path})`, { cause: error })
380	  }
381	}

3	 * {@link COMPOSITION_FILE}, optionally beside a {@link METADATA_FILE} carrying
4	 * its display text; the directory name is the preset id. Discovery
5	 * re-reads the roots on every call so a preset authored while the process is
6	 * running is visible without a restart.
7	 *
8	 * Discovery also owns preset HEALTH: a directory whose composition is
9	 * missing or unloadable is reported as a broken roster row rather than
10	 * skipped. A skipped directory would still occupy its id on disk — the copy
11	 * path refuses the name while no surface shows anything to delete — and a
12	 * malformed composition would otherwise read as an ordinary preset until the
13	 * first session fails to mount it.
14	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/discovery
15	 */

17	import { readdir, readFile, stat } from 'node:fs/promises'
18	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
19	import { load } from 'js-yaml'
20	import { entryListSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
21	import { expandHomePath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths'
22	import { readPresetMetadata } from './metadata.ts'
23	import { PRESET_ID, type AgentPreset, type PresetRoot } from './preset.ts'

25	/** The composition file that makes a directory a preset. */
26	export const COMPOSITION_FILE = 'agent.cordis.yml'
27	
28	/**
29	 * Harness-home directory holding locally authored presets.
30	 *
31	 * This package owns the writable root the way `dsh-skill-filesystem` owns
32	 * `<dshHome>/skills`. An app must assemble the SHIPPED root, whose path only
33	 * the installed app can resolve; where a person's own presets go is the same
34	 * place in every deployment that does not say otherwise, so a launcher that
35	 * forgets to configure one still finds them.
36	 *
37	 * Package-internal on purpose: no consumer outside this package addresses the
38	 * directory by name, and a test that imported it could not catch this value
39	 * being wrong — the expected segment is spelled out where it is asserted.
40	 */
41	export const USER_PRESET_DIR = '.agent-presets'
42	
43	/**
44	 * Why `rows` cannot be an entry list, or undefined when it can.
45	 *
46	 * A shallow shape check, deliberately short of the loader's work: it does not
47	 * resolve plugin names or apply configs. What it catches is the hand-edit
48	 * that produces a file the loader cannot even begin with — and it must accept
49	 * everything the loader accepts, which is why rows are only required to be
50	 * maps carrying a plugin `name` (groups recurse into their own lists).
51	 * @param rows - the parsed composition document.
52	 * @param at - row-path prefix for nested diagnostics, empty at the top level.
53	 * @returns one human-readable reason, or undefined when the shape holds.
54	 */
55	function entryListProblem(rows: unknown, at = ''): string | undefined {
56	  if (!Array.isArray(rows)) {
57	    return at === ''
58	      ? 'the composition must be a top-level list of plugin rows'
59	      : `group ${at} must hold a list of plugin rows`
60	  }
61	  for (const [index, row] of rows.entries()) {
62	    const label = at === '' ? `row ${String(index + 1)}` : `${at} row ${String(index + 1)}`
63	    if (typeof row !== 'object' || row === null || Array.isArray(row)) {
64	      return `${label} is not a plugin row (expected a map with a "name")`
65	    }
66	    const { name, group, config } = row as { name?: unknown; group?: unknown; config?: unknown }
67	    if (typeof name !== 'string' || name === '') {
68	      return `${label} names no plugin (a "name" string is required)`
69	    }
70	    if (group === true) {
71	      const nested = entryListProblem(config, label)
72	      if (nested !== undefined) return nested
73	    }
74	  }
75	  return undefined
76	}
77	
78	/**
79	 * Why the composition at `path` cannot mount, or undefined when it looks
80	 * loadable. Parsed with the loader's own YAML dialect ({@link entryListSchema},
81	 * the one carrying `!!js`), so health can never call a composition broken
82	 * that the loader would accept.
83	 * @param path - absolute path of the composition file.
84	 * @returns one human-readable reason, or undefined when the file is loadable.
85	 */
86	async function compositionProblem(path: string): Promise<string | undefined> {
87	  let content: string
88	  try {
89	    content = await readFile(path, 'utf8')
90	  } catch {
91	    // The caller statted this file moments ago; any read failure now —
92	    // deleted in between, permissions — is the same answer as unparsable.
93	    return `the composition file ${COMPOSITION_FILE} cannot be read`
94	  }
95	  let rows: unknown
96	  try {
97	    rows = load(content, { schema: entryListSchema })
98	  } catch (error) {
99	    /* v8 ignore next -- js-yaml throws YAMLException (an Error) for every parse failure; the fallback keeps a hostile value readable */
100	    const full = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
101	    // First line only: js-yaml appends a multi-line code-frame snippet, and
102	    // the reason is displayed on a roster card, not in a terminal.
103	    return `the composition is not valid YAML: ${full.replace(/\n[\s\S]*$/, '')}`
104	  }
105	  return entryListProblem(rows)
106	}
107	
108	/**
109	 * Whether `path` names an existing regular file.
110	 * @param path - absolute path to test.
111	 * @returns true when the path resolves to a file.
112	 */
113	async function isFile(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
114	  try {
115	    return (await stat(path)).isFile()
116	  } catch {
117	    // Any stat failure — absent, unreadable, a dangling link — means this
118	    // directory does not present a composition, which is not an error: the
119	    // directory simply is not a preset.
120	    return false
121	  }
122	}

124	/**
125	 * Scan one root for preset directories.
126	 *
127	 * An absent root yields no presets rather than throwing: the user root does
128	 * not exist until the first locally authored preset, and naming a default
129	 * that no root supplies already fails loud at resolution.
130	 *
131	 * Every directory whose name is a usable preset id is a roster row — broken
132	 * when its composition is missing or unloadable. A directory named outside
133	 * {@link PRESET_ID} is skipped instead: no copy could ever claim that name,
134	 * so it blocks nothing, and reporting `.DS_Store`-grade residue as broken
135	 * presets would teach users to ignore the marker.
136	 * @param root - the directory and the trust its presets inherit.
137	 * @returns the root's presets ordered by id.
138	 */
139	export async function scanRoot(root: PresetRoot): Promise<AgentPreset[]> {
140	  const dir = resolve(expandHomePath(root.path))
141	  let children
142	  try {
143	    children = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
144	  } catch (error) {
145	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return []
146	    throw new Error(`agent-presets: cannot read preset root ${dir}: ${String(error)}`, { cause: error })
147	  }
148	  const found: AgentPreset[] = []
149	  for (const child of children) {
150	    if (!child.isDirectory() || !PRESET_ID.test(child.name)) continue
151	    const directory = join(dir, child.name)
152	    const path = join(directory, COMPOSITION_FILE)
153	    const broken = await isFile(path)
154	      ? await compositionProblem(path)
155	      : `the composition file ${COMPOSITION_FILE} is missing — the directory still occupies the id; delete it or restore the file`
156	    // Display text only, and never fatal: a preset with unreadable metadata
157	    // still mounts, it just shows its id.
158	    const metadata = await readPresetMetadata(directory)
159	    found.push({
160	      id: child.name, trust: root.trust, path, ...metadata,
161	      ...broken === undefined ? {} : { broken },
162	    })
163	  }
164	  // Declared order first so the shipped set reads by capability; everything
165	  // else falls back to the id, which keeps authored presets stable.
166	  return found.sort((left, right) => {
167	    const byOrder = (left.order ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) - (right.order ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)
168	    return byOrder === 0 ? left.id.localeCompare(right.id) : byOrder
169	  })
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Scan every root in precedence order.
174	 * @param roots - roots in precedence order; an earlier root wins a duplicate id.
175	 * @returns every discovered preset, first-root-wins per id.
176	 */
177	export async function discoverPresets(roots: readonly PresetRoot[]): Promise<AgentPreset[]> {
178	  const byId = new Map<string, AgentPreset>()
179	  for (const root of roots) {
180	    for (const preset of await scanRoot(root)) {
181	      if (byId.has(preset.id)) continue
182	      byId.set(preset.id, preset)
183	    }
184	  }
185	  return [...byId.values()]
186	}

262	  /**
263	   * Compose one agent from a preset: ensure the preset's standing mount, then
264	   * parent the agent's scope key to it so the mount's registrations and
265	   * listeners cover this agent.
266	   *
267	   * Call from the agent factory's `setup(agentCtx)`; a rejection there rolls
268	   * the agent creation back, so a broken preset never yields a half-composed
269	   * session.
270	   * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context.
271	   * @param id - the preset id, or `undefined` for {@link defaultId}.
272	   * @returns the preset that was composed, for the caller to record.
273	   * @throws when the preset is unknown or its composition is unusable.
274	   */
275	  async mount(agentCtx: Context, id?: string): Promise<AgentPreset> {
276	    const agentKey = scopeOf(agentCtx)
277	    if (agentKey === undefined) {
278	      throw new Error('agent-presets: refusing to compose an unscoped context; the scope key is what joins an agent to its preset')
279	    }
280	    const preset = await this.resolveMountable(id)
281	    const standing = await this.ensureStanding(preset)
282	    // The one bind of this agent's ancestry. The binding is the only re-link
283	    // authority, held privately so nothing outside this roster can move a
284	    // composed agent to another preset; a later recompose layer re-links
285	    // through it under the caller-owned blank-session contract.
286	    this.bindings.set(agentKey, bindScopeParent(agentKey, standing.key))
287	    return preset
288	  }
289	
290	  /**
291	   * Join one agent to the SAME standing composition another already runs on.
292	   *
293	   * This is how a child agent inherits its parent's capabilities. It is a bind,
294	   * not a mount: the parent's generation is already composed, so the child gets
295	   * that exact instance — the same plugin objects, the same tool registrations,
296	   * the same prompt sections. Re-resolving the parent's preset by id instead
297	   * would re-read the roster, and a composition file edited since the parent
298	   * started would hand the child a DIFFERENT generation than the one its
299	   * parent's history was produced under (and a preset deleted since would fail
300	   * the child outright while its parent keeps running).
301	   *
302	   * Synchronous, and with no composition failure mode of its own — it reads no
303	   * roster, mounts nothing, and touches no file — which is what lets a child
304	   * creation window use it: the two in-process subagent drivers compose their
305	   * children inside a synchronous `setup`. It still rejects a caller error, as
306	   * the `@throws` below record.
307	   *
308	   * A parent that joined no preset — a rosterless deployment — yields no join
309	   * and no error: there, the model-facing rows sit in the host composition and
310	   * the child already sees them through the global layer.
311	   * @param agentCtx - the joining agent's scope context.
312	   * @param parentCtx - the scope context of the agent whose composition to join.
313	   * @returns the preset id joined, or undefined when the parent joined none.
314	   * @throws when `agentCtx` carries no scope, or has already joined a preset.
315	   */
316	  composeFrom(agentCtx: Context, parentCtx: Context): string | undefined {
317	    const agentKey = scopeOf(agentCtx)
318	    if (agentKey === undefined) {
319	      throw new Error('agent-presets: refusing to compose an unscoped context; the scope key is what joins an agent to its preset')
320	    }
321	    const standing = standingMountFor(parentCtx)
322	    if (standing === undefined) return undefined
323	    this.bindings.set(agentKey, bindScopeParent(agentKey, standing.key))
324	    return standing.presetId
325	  }
326	
327	  /**
328	   * The preset one live agent runs on.
329	   *
330	   * Read from the live scope chain rather than from the session, so it answers
331	   * for an agent whose session has not recorded a preset yet — a child agent
332	   * whose durable header is being built from its parent's composition.
333	   * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context.
334	   * @returns the preset id, or undefined when the agent joined none.
335	   */
336	  composedPreset(agentCtx: Context): string | undefined {
337	    return standingMountFor(agentCtx)?.presetId
338	  }

340	  /**
341	   * The roots this roster scans, which is not `config.roots`: it is every
342	   * configured root in order, then the harness-home user root unless
343	   * `includeUserRoot` is false. Read this — not the config field — to answer
344	   * whether a roster is composed at all, so one derivation decides it.
345	   */
346	  get roots(): readonly PresetRoot[] {
347	    return this.resolvedRoots
348	  }

350	  /** Whether this deployment has a root locally authored presets go to. */
351	  get authorable(): boolean {
352	    return this.resolvedRoots.some(root => root.trust === 'user')
353	  }
354	
355	  /**
356	   * Read one preset's composition text.
357	   * @param id - the preset id.
358	   * @returns the composition exactly as stored.
359	   * @throws when no configured root supplies that id.
360	   */
361	  async read(id: string): Promise<string> {
362	    return await readComposition(await this.resolve(id))
363	  }
364	
365	  /**
366	   * Create a locally authored preset by copying an existing one whole.
367	   *
368	   * Copy is the only authoring write. Composition text never crosses this
369	   * seam: the source is named by id and its directory is copied as it stands,
370	   * so the copy is exactly as loadable as its source and authoring grants no
371	   * capability the roster did not already carry. The copy is NOT mounted to
372	   * validate — a source that mounts today yields a copy that mounts today.
373	   * @param from - the preset the copy starts from; shipped presets are the
374	   * primary source, so any trust is accepted.
375	   * @param id - the new preset's id, which becomes its directory name.
376	   * @param name - display name for the copy; absent falls back to the id.
377	   * @throws when the source is unknown, the id is unusable or already taken,
378	   * or the deployment configures no writable root.
379	   */
380	  async copy(from: string, id: string, name?: string): Promise<void> {
381	    const source = await this.resolve(from)
382	    // The roster check refuses ids any root supplies — shipped ones included,
383	    // since a user directory named like a shipped preset is shadowed by it.
384	    // The disk check inside copyComposition only sees the writable root.
385	    if ((await this.list()).some(preset => preset.id === id)) {
386	      throw new PresetExistsError(id)
387	    }
388	    await copyComposition(this.resolvedRoots, source, id, name)
389	    // A settled mount under this id can only be stale (its preset was deleted
390	    // from disk outside `remove`); the new preset must not inherit it. Every
391	    // session already joined keeps the generation it runs on regardless.
392	    this.standing.delete(id)
393	  }
394	
395	  /**
396	   * Delete a locally authored preset.
397	   * @param id - the preset id.
398	   * @throws when the preset is unknown or ships with the deployment.
399	   */
400	  async remove(id: string): Promise<void> {
401	    await deleteComposition(this.resolvedRoots, await this.resolve(id))
402	    // Sessions on the deleted preset keep their standing mount; only new
403	    // sessions see the roster without it.
404	    this.standing.delete(id)
405	    // Storing a default that does not exist YET is deliberate — the roster is a
406	    // live directory, so a name absent now may exist by the time a session asks
407	    // for it, and `resolve` reports it then. A default this call just deleted is
408	    // not that case: nothing will ever supply it again, and left in place every
409	    // session created without an explicit pick would fail to start. Clearing it
410	    // exposes the deployment's own default underneath, which is the layering.
411	    if (this.settings?.get().default !== id) return
412	    await this.settingsService?.mutate(
413	      settingsNamespace(SETTINGS_NAMESPACE),
414	      [{ op: 'unset', path: ['default'] }],
415	    )
416	  }
417	
418	  /**
419	   * One agent's instance of a service its preset mounted.
420	   *
421	   * A preset publishes services behind `isolate` realms, which are invisible
422	   * outside the group that declares them — including to the host. This is how a
423	   * caller holding the agent reads one anyway: a request that is ABOUT a
424	   * session but arrives from outside it, which is every browser RPC.
425	   *
426	   * Read addressing only. A host row that `inject`s a service cannot use this,
427	   * because injection resolves before any session exists and has no agent to
428	   * key by; such a service belongs on the host plane instead.
429	   * @param agent - the agent whose composition to look inside.
430	   * @param name - the service name as the preset's rows resolve it.
431	   * @returns the agent's instance, or undefined when its preset mounts none.
432	   */
433	  serviceFor<K extends string & keyof Context>(agent: { ctx: Context }, name: K): Context[K] | undefined {
434	    return serviceForAgent(this.ctx, agent, name)
435	  }
436	
437	  /**
438	   * Re-link one agent to a different preset's standing composition.
439	   *
440	   * Only valid while the agent has produced nothing: swapping tools mid
441	   * conversation would leave logged tool calls the new composition cannot
442	   * make. The CALLER owns that check — this method does not read session
443	   * history.
444	   *
445	   * The swap is a parent re-link, not an unmount: standing mounts are shared
446	   * and permanent, so the old composition stays for its other agents and the
447	   * new one is ensured BEFORE the link moves. An unknown or unusable preset
448	   * therefore throws with the agent exactly as it was — there is no torn-down
449	   * state to restore. The re-link runs through the binding this roster kept
450	   * from the agent's mount — dsh-scope's only re-link authority. An agent
451	   * that never composed one has nothing to re-link: the switch is then the
452	   * agent's first bind, exactly a mount.
453	   * @param agentCtx - the agent's scope context.
454	   * @param id - the preset to compose the agent from instead.
455	   * @returns the preset now installed.
456	   * @throws when the preset is unknown or its composition is unusable.
457	   */
458	  async recompose(agentCtx: Context, id: string): Promise<AgentPreset> {
459	    const agentKey = scopeOf(agentCtx)
460	    if (agentKey === undefined) {
461	      throw new Error('agent-presets: refusing to recompose an unscoped context')
462	    }
463	    const preset = await this.resolveMountable(id)
464	    const standing = await this.ensureStanding(preset)
465	    const binding = this.bindings.get(agentKey)
466	    if (binding === undefined) {
467	      this.bindings.set(agentKey, bindScopeParent(agentKey, standing.key))
468	    } else {
469	      binding.rebind(standing.key)
470	    }
471	    return preset
472	  }
473	
474	  /**
475	   * The standing scope key of one preset, for a host reader with no agent.
476	   *
477	   * A cold transcript read resolves tool presenters against the composition
478	   * the session recorded, and the standing mount makes that possible without
479	   * resuming anything: ensuring the mount composes plugins but starts no
480	   * agent, no session, and no turn.
481	   * @param id - the preset id, or `undefined` for {@link defaultId}.
482	   * @returns the standing scope key readers pass as a registry view scope.
483	   * @throws when the preset is unknown or its composition is unusable.
484	   */
485	  async standingKeyFor(id?: string): Promise<ScopeKey> {
486	    const preset = await this.resolveMountable(id)
487	    return (await this.ensureStanding(preset)).key
488	  }
489	
490	  /** Resolve (or create, single-flight) the standing mount of one preset. */
491	  private async ensureStanding(preset: AgentPreset): Promise<StandingMount> {
492	    const pending = this.standing.get(preset.id)
493	    if (pending !== undefined) {
494	      const mounted = await pending
495	      // Files are the only composition editor (authoring is copy/delete), so
496	      // the stamp is what notices an edit: a changed file starts the next
497	      // generation here, for this and later sessions. An unreadable stamp
498	      // serves the current generation — a mount must survive its file
499	      // disappearing, and failing the session over a stat would not.
500	      const current = await compositionStamp(preset.path)
501	      if (current === undefined || sameStamp(mounted.stamp, current)) return mounted
502	      // TODO: reclaim the superseded generation once the last agent joined to
503	      // it is gone. The subtree is not inert — `dsh-skill-filesystem` watches its
504	      // roots — and the settings-page authoring flow turns "a composition
505	      // changed" into a per-save event. This needs a joined-agent count on
506	      // StandingMount, incremented in `mount`/`composeFrom`/`recompose` and
507	      // decremented when the agent's scope key dies.
508	      // Guarded delete: a caller that raced this one may have already started
509	      // the next generation, and dropping THAT pointer would fork a third.
510	      if (this.standing.get(preset.id) === pending) this.standing.delete(preset.id)
511	      return this.ensureStanding(preset)
512	    }
513	    const created = (async (): Promise<StandingMount> => {
514	      const key: ScopeKey = { agentPreset: preset.id }
515	      const scope = createScope(this.selfCtx, key)
516	      try {
517	        // Stamped before the file is read: an edit racing the mount makes the
518	        // stamp stale rather than silently current, so the next session
519	        // refreshes instead of trusting a composition older than its stamp.
520	        const stamp = await compositionStamp(preset.path)
521	        if (stamp === undefined) {
522	          throw new PresetMountError(preset.id, `composition file is unreadable: ${preset.path}`)
523	        }
524	        await mountPreset(scope.ctx, preset)
525	        return { key, scope, stamp }
526	      } catch (error) {
527	        this.standing.delete(preset.id)
528	        await scope.dispose()
529	        throw error
530	      }
531	    })()
532	    this.standing.set(preset.id, created)
533	    return created
534	  }
535	}
536	
537	/** The composition file identity one standing generation was mounted from. */
538	interface CompositionStamp {
539	  /** Modification time in milliseconds, as `stat` reports it. */
540	  readonly mtimeMs: number
541	  /** File size in bytes, the tiebreak for edits within one mtime tick. */
542	  readonly size: number
543	}
544	
545	/** Read one composition file's stamp, or undefined when it cannot be statted. */
546	async function compositionStamp(path: string): Promise<CompositionStamp | undefined> {
547	  try {
548	    const { mtimeMs, size } = await stat(path)
549	    return { mtimeMs, size }
550	  } catch {
551	    // Deleted, replaced by an unreadable entry, or otherwise unstattable all
552	    // mean the same to the caller: the file offers no identity to compare.
553	    return undefined
554	  }
555	}
556	
557	/** Whether two stamps name the same file state. */
558	function sameStamp(a: CompositionStamp, b: CompositionStamp): boolean {
559	  return a.mtimeMs === b.mtimeMs && a.size === b.size
560	}
561	
562	/** One preset's standing composition. */
563	interface StandingMount {
564	  /** Scope key agents are parented to; also the mount's registration scope. */
565	  readonly key: ScopeKey
566	  /** Disposal boundary; held for whole-tree teardown, never per-session. */
567	  readonly scope: Scope
568	  /** Stamp of the composition file this generation was mounted from. */
569	  readonly stamp: CompositionStamp
570	}
571	
572	export default AgentPresets

1	/**
2	 * Event-only filesystem read policy; it registers no service and declares no
3	 * config, because every deployment-varying value belongs to `ctx.readBarrier`.
4	 * It is the read counterpart of the write and edit policy
5	 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy` contributes through the same `fs/*`
6	 * event gate: it decides `fs/read-intent`, refusing a target the barrier denies
7	 * to the calling session's role and delegating every other read. See the
8	 * package README for composition rules.
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import type { FsReadDenial, FsTarget } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
14	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
15	import type { Session } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import type { FsReadBarrierActor } from './types.ts'
17	
18	export type * from './types.ts'
19	
20	/**
21	 * The complete model-facing account of one refused read. No recovery
22	 * instruction follows it: no retry of the same call succeeds.
23	 * @param displayPath - the model-facing path of the refused target.
24	 * @returns the exact denial message.
25	 */
26	export function readBarrierDenialMessage(displayPath: string): string {
27	  return `read denied: "${displayPath}" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it`
28	}
29	
30	/**
31	 * Find the session a read runs for by narrowing the opaque event actor.
32	 * @param actor - the tool-execution context the read executor dispatched with.
33	 * @returns the calling session, or `undefined` for a call with no agent.
34	 */
35	function sessionOf(actor: object | undefined): Session | undefined {
36	  // tsgolint treats object as assignable to weak FsReadBarrierActor, while tsc still requires the structural cast for property access.
37	  // See the analyzer-divergence consequence in .agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-29-oxlint-linter.md.
38	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion -- The analyzers disagree on this weak type.
39	  return (actor as FsReadBarrierActor | undefined)?.agent?.session
40	}
41	
42	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
43	export const name = 'fs-read-barrier'
44	
45	/** The barrier owns every deployment-varying value this plugin decides from. */
46	export const inject = ['readBarrier']
47	
48	/**
49	 * Decide one dispatched read.
50	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the barrier service.
51	 * @param target - the resolved target the executor is about to read.
52	 * @param actor - the opaque tool-execution context.
53	 * @returns the refusal, or `undefined` to delegate to the next read policy.
54	 */
55	async function decide(ctx: Context, target: FsTarget, actor: object | undefined): Promise<FsReadDenial | undefined> {
56	  const session = sessionOf(actor)
57	  if (session === undefined) return undefined
58	  const policy = ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })
59	  if (!await ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)) return undefined
60	  const denial = ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, 'fs', target)
61	  return { code: 'FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED', message: readBarrierDenialMessage(denial.displayPath) }
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Register the `fs/read-intent` listener.
66	 * @param ctx - the plugin context; the registration is an effect scoped to it.
67	 */
68	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
69	  // Delegating, not single-slot: a barrier that owned the slot would stop every
70	  // later read policy from deciding. The waterfall is unbound (the executor
71	  // dispatches it with no `this`), so the listener takes the raw arguments.
72	  ctx.on('fs/read-intent', async (target, actor, next) => await decide(ctx, target, actor) ?? await next())
73	}

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Test driver: boot the read-barrier composition, reserve the barrier's run
 * directory for one of two sessions, then read the same validator-owned file
 * from the implementer session, from a session holding no reservation, and
 * directly through `ctx.fs` as a trusted plugin. It reports every outcome plus
 * the implementer's durable refusal records for the e2e's assertions.
 */

import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
import { CallId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'

const configPath = process.argv[2]
if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('read-barrier driver requires a config path')

const signal = new AbortController().signal
let calls = 0

/** Execute the `read` tool exactly as the agent loop does, and flatten the outcome. */
async function read(ctx: Context, agent: Agent, path: string) {
  const result = await ctx.tools.execute({
    signal,
    callId: CallId(`read-${++calls}`),
    name: 'read',
    arguments: { file_path: path },
    agent,
  })
  return {
    isError: result.isError,
    code: result.error?.info?.code,
    text: result.content.flatMap(block => (block.type === 'text' ? [block.text] : [])).join(''),
  }
}

const ctx = await boot('read-barrier-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
try {
  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the driver creates agents only over the settled application.
  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
  const barrier = ctx.get('readBarrier')
  if (barrier === undefined) throw new Error('read-barrier driver requires the barrier service')

  const agentOptions = { provider: 'cli-mock', model: 'cli-mock' }
  const implementer = await ctx.agents.create({ sessionId: SessionId('read-barrier-implementer'), meta: { cwd: process.cwd() }, agentOptions })
  const validator = await ctx.agents.create({ sessionId: SessionId('read-barrier-validator'), meta: { cwd: process.cwd() }, agentOptions })
  try {
    const runDirectory = barrier.reserve(implementer.agent)
    await mkdir(join(runDirectory, 'checks'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
    const check = join(runDirectory, 'checks', 'marker')
    await writeFile(check, 'test -f MARKER\n', { mode: 0o600 })
    const workspaceFile = join(process.cwd(), 'work.txt')
    await writeFile(workspaceFile, 'implementer work\n')

    const implementerCheck = await read(ctx, implementer.agent, check)
    const implementerWorkspace = await read(ctx, implementer.agent, workspaceFile)
    const validatorCheck = await read(ctx, validator.agent, check)
    // A trusted plugin reads the same target directly: the barrier denies at the
    // executor, never by removing the capability.
    const trustedRead = await ctx.fs.readText(await ctx.fs.resolve(check))

/**
 * Test-only validator stand-in: seed one validator-owned file under the barrier
 * root and reserve the run directory of every agent the composition creates, so
 * the snapshot's single session holds the implementer role from its first turn.
 */

import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'

export const name = 'reserve-implementer'
export const inject = ['agents', 'readBarrier']

/** The standard a validator would place under its own root before the run starts. */
const STANDARD = '{\n  "checks": [\n    { "id": "marker", "run": "test -f MARKER" }\n  ]\n}\n'

/**
 * Seed the validator-owned standard and reserve every agent. Loader siblings
 * mount concurrently, so the sweep covers an agent the spine created before this
 * plugin's listener existed.
 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the agent registry and the barrier.
 */
export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
  writeFileSync(join(ctx.readBarrier.root, 'standard.json'), STANDARD, { mode: 0o600 })
  for (const agent of ctx.agents.list()) ctx.readBarrier.reserve(agent)
  ctx.on('agent/created', ({ agent }) => { ctx.readBarrier.reserve(agent) })
}

224	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
225	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
226	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
227	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
228	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
229	  const marker = '\n…'
230	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
231	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
232	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
233	}

235	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
236	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
237	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
238	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
239	  const lines = [`${exit}${cause}`]
240	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
241	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
242	  return bound(lines.join('\n'), maxChars)
243	}

259	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
260	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
261	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
262	  ))
263	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
264	  const total: TokenUsage = {
265	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
266	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
267	  }
268	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
269	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
270	      const value = step[key]
271	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
272	    })
273	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)

345	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
346	  private async drive(
347	    agent: Agent,
348	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
349	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
350	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
351	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
352	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
353	    await agent.whenIdle()

355	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
356	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {

358	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
359	    })
360	    goals.disarm(agent)
361	    completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
362	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
363	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
364	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
365	    try {
366	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
367	        agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
368	        await agent.whenIdle()
369	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
370	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
371	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard)
372	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts)
373	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
374	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
375	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
376	          executor: 'runner',
377	          treeHash,
378	        })
379	        if (outcome.certified) {
380	          certificate = outcome.certificate
381	          const current = goals.get(agent)
382	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
383	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
384	          }
385	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
386	          break
387	        }
388	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
389	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
390	        prompt = followupText(directive)
391	      }
392	    } finally {
393	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
394	    }
395	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
396	    return {
397	      environment: definition.id,
398	      sessionId: agent.id,
399	      stamp,
400	      attempts,
401	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
402	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
403	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
404	    }
405	  }

407	  /** The standard the run measures; the implementer cannot mutate it, so another goal's standard or none is an anomaly. */
408	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
409	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
410	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {
411	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the standard for goal "${goalId}" is no longer current`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST')
412	    }
413	    return standard
414	  }

416	  /**
417	   * Reserve the run's validator-owned directory and stock what the checks read
418	   * from it. Without a composed barrier there is no reservation and the checks
419	   * run their instructions inline, exactly as the run's declared isolation says.
420	   * @param agent - the implementer agent this run drives.
421	   * @param definition - the environment being run, supplying the held-out fixture.
422	   * @returns the reservation, or `undefined` when no barrier is composed.
423	   */
424	  private async reserve(agent: Agent, definition: EnvironmentDefinition): Promise<string | undefined> {
425	    const barrier = this.ctx.get('readBarrier')
426	    if (barrier === undefined) return undefined
427	    const runDirectory = barrier.reserve(agent)
428	    // A held-out environment's fixture is evaluation material: the copy under
429	    // the reservation is the one an inspecting validator reads, never the
430	    // workspace overlay the implementer works in.
431	    if (definition.heldOut && definition.task.fixture !== undefined) {
432	      await cp(definition.task.fixture, join(runDirectory, FIXTURE_DIR), { recursive: true })
433	    }
434	    return runDirectory
435	  }

437	  /**
438	   * Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the
439	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
440	   * instruction inline.
441	   */
442	  private async execute(
443	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
444	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
445	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
446	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
447	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
448	    for (const check of checks) {
449	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
450	      const spec = this.ctx.shell.resolve({
451	        command: script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`,
452	        workdir: request.workspace,
453	        timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
454	        signal: request.signal,
455	      })
456	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(spec)
457	      results.push({
458	        checkId: check.id,
459	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
460	        evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
461	      })
462	    }
463	    return results
464	  }

99	    parameters: {

108	
109	  ctx.tools.register(defineTool({

111	    description: 'Read one full unabridged event and optional neighboring raw-event summaries from an authorized session.',
112	    parameters: {
113	      ...toolInput.targetSessionParameter,
114	      seq: { type: 'integer', required: true, description: 'Target event sequence number.' },
115	      before: { type: 'integer', description: 'Number of preceding raw events to summarize. Omit for none.' },
116	      after: { type: 'integer', description: 'Number of following raw events to summarize. Omit for none.' },
117	    },
118	    output: TEXT_OUTPUT,
119	    isConcurrencySafe: () => true,
120	    execute: (args, exec) => operations.executeEventRead(ctx, args, exec),
121	    presentCall: args => presentation.presentEventTargetCall('Read event', args),
122	  }))
123	}
124	
125	function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
126	  const maxSearchResults = config.maxSearchResults ?? DEFAULT_MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS
127	  const searchTimeoutMs = config.searchTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS
128	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxSearchResults) || maxSearchResults < 1) {
129	    throw new TypeError('tool-session-query: maxSearchResults must be a positive safe integer')
130	  }
131	  if (!Number.isInteger(searchTimeoutMs) || searchTimeoutMs < 1 || searchTimeoutMs > MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS) {
132	    throw new TypeError(
133	      `tool-session-query: searchTimeoutMs must be a positive integer no greater than ${MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS}`,
134	    )
135	  }
136	  return { maxSearchResults, searchTimeoutMs }
137	}

2	 * The session-log record of which preset a session actually runs.
3	 *
4	 * The creation header names the preset a session STARTED with, and it is
5	 * deep-frozen because that is a creation fact. A session may still change
6	 * preset while it is blank, and the effect of that change outlives the blank
7	 * window: the first turn — and every turn after it — runs under the newly
8	 * mounted composition. Recording the change is what keeps the log honest, and
9	 * it is required outright by the repo's model-visible ⟺ logged rule, since the
10	 * preset decides the tool schemas and prompt sections the model sees.
11	 *
12	 * Reconstruction reads {@link resolveSessionPreset}, never the header alone.
13	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/session
14	 */

16	import type { SessionEvent, SessionHeader } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
17	
18	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
19	  interface SessionEventMap {
20	    /**
21	     * The session's agent preset was chosen after creation, while the session
22	     * was still blank. Log-only: it records the composition later turns ran
23	     * under, so a resumed or forked session rebuilds the same one instead of
24	     * the header's creation-time value.
25	     */
26	    'agent-preset/selected': { agentPreset: string }
27	  }
28	}

30	/** The minimum a caller must supply to resolve a session's preset. */
31	export interface PresetBearingSession {
32	  /** The session's creation header. */
33	  readonly header: SessionHeader
34	  /** The session's event log, oldest first. */
35	  readonly events: readonly SessionEvent[]
36	}

38	/**
39	 * The preset a session actually runs, newest selection winning.
40	 *
41	 * The header supplies the creation-time value; every later selection is a
42	 * logged event, so the last one is the answer. Reading the header alone
43	 * rebuilds a switched session under the composition it was created with, not
44	 * the one its history was produced under.
45	 * @param session - the session's header and event log.
46	 * @returns the preset id, or `undefined` when the deployment composes none.
47	 */
48	export function resolveSessionPreset(session: PresetBearingSession): string | undefined {
49	  for (let index = session.events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
50	    const event = session.events[index]
51	    if (event?.type === 'agent-preset/selected') return event.data.agentPreset
52	  }
53	  return session.header.agentPreset
